messages.subject: "Attaching package :" how to make sure this happens?
parts:
If I runApp() locally in the directory where I developed the app, it works fine.  I also get the message:

Attaching package: ‘<packagename>'


If I deployApp() the app, it deploys successfully, but the application fails to start.  An error message is shown.  See https://kenkleinman.shinyapps.io/MatchingApp/


Testing shows that if I copy the contents of app.R to a new (clean) directory, and runApp() from there, the 

Attaching package: ‘<packagename>'

message is absent, and the error message I receive is identical to the one shown on the link above.


Apologies if this is an obvious question, but apparently, this particular package is not attaching correctly, whatever that means, in shiny parlance.  How can I make that happen?  And why would it happen only in the directory where the app was originally built?  FWIW, I didn't build it myself but am using a github repos of something built by someone else.  I can deploy the Old Faithful app.

parts:
Hi Joshua--

Thanks for reminding me to check the obvious, which I had not in fact done.

Note that I tried compiling the app in another directory _on the same computer_ and got the same error as when I try to upload to shinyapp.io.  So it would appear unlikely to be an error having to do with platform issues.  And, in fact, I specify no paths and don't change the working directory.  I also don't access any data sets, though the user can upload Excel files.

I don't believe there are any Windows-only programs-- though, again, I can replicate the problem on the same computer, so it doesn't seem likely to be a platform issue.  I don't think there are any Tcl/Tk packages... again, hard to see how I could generate the same error on my own machine, if that were the case.

FTR, what I get when I try to compile the app on the same computer but in a different directory closely resembles what you have here:

Warning in is.na(max) :
is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
Error in if (!is.na(max)) inputTag$attribs$max = max :
argument is of length zero

which is identical to that shown on the link to the app.

AFAICT, the warning and error are related, and are likely deeply internal to the package that isn't shown as "attaching".  I used devtools::session_info() and couldn't see meaningful differences between when it would and would not compile.

Any thoughts?
